SqlVectorTypeSupport.summary: Specifies the level of support for the vector data type which the driver negotiates with the server.

remarks.para: A vector column is returned in its binary form when the server acknowledges a version of the vector feature extension which covers the column's base type. A column whose base type is not covered is returned as a varchar(max) containing a JSON array.

Starting with Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 8.0, the default is . On .NET, successful V2 negotiation changes the result of GetValue for a vector column with a float16 base type from a JSON string to SqlVector<Half>. Set Vector Type Support=v1 to preserve the JSON string representation.

Off.summary: The vector feature extension is not requested. Every vector column is returned as a varchar(max) containing a JSON array, as it was before the type existed.

V1.summary: Vectors with a float32 base type are returned in their binary form and are surfaced as SqlVector<float>. Columns with any other base type are returned as a varchar(max) containing a JSON array.

summary.para: Adds float16 to the base types returned in their binary form. This is the default starting with Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 8.0. On .NET, a vector column with a float16 base type is surfaced as SqlVector<System.Half>; on .NET Framework, where System.Half is unavailable, it is surfaced as a JSON array string and can be read as a SqlVector<float> on request.

The column representations above describe reader results. Output parameters follow their client-side binding: on .NET Framework, a SqlVector<float> binding returns a SqlVector<float>, while a varchar(max) binding returns JSON text. For non-null text output, Value is a string and SqlValue is a SqlString.

On .NET Framework, the driver widens each element of a vector column with a float16 base type to float32 as it reads, and renders the result as a JSON array for the string read paths. On .NET, a SqlVector<Half> wraps the payload the server sent, so no per-element conversion takes place. Take this into account when you choose this value for a .NET Framework application which reads vector columns with a float16 base type in bulk.
